title: The wizard's write-nothing-before-every-prompt invariant now has an exception and nothing enforces which side a new prompt lands on
description:
Found during LCLI-466's implementation review, outside its acceptance criteria.

Before LCLI-466 the interactive wizard held a clean invariant, commented explicitly at the call site in src/commands/init.ts and attributed to LCLI-358.1: EVERY wizard question is asked before the first byte is written, so an EOF, a declined git prompt or a rejected flag combination leaves the directory exactly as the run found it, .git included.

LCLI-466 necessarily adds a prompt AFTER the base scaffold, because an id collision cannot be known until the migration actually runs. That is correct in this instance -- the migration is the write that failed, and Quest wrote nothing -- but the invariant's comment now describes a rule with one unstated exception, and nothing distinguishes a legitimate post-write prompt from an accidental one. The next person to add a prompt has no way to tell which side of the line they are on except by reading the comment and judging.

The task is to state the rule rather than leave it to a reader to notice: say what makes a post-write prompt legitimate (it recovers from a failure whose own write did not land), update the call-site comment so it stops asserting a universal it no longer has, and decide whether anything can enforce it -- a test that asserts the on-disk state at each prompt boundary is the obvious candidate. Prefer a check over a comment, per the fleet's standing preference for removing judgement over documenting it.

Related: the same 'put the exception in the claim, not two paragraphs down' problem the SDLC guidance calls out for prose, occurring here in a code comment.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A test asserts, at every wizard prompt boundary rather than only after the run, that the directory is still untouched: test/init.test.ts "no wizard question is asked after the first byte is written", carrying a positive control that the run both asked (prompts recorded > 0) and wrote (created > 0), and proven to reject by a mutant that records one post-write snapshot.

The call-site comments in src/commands/init.ts state the invariant as a universal again and name the mechanism that guarantees it — applyBaseScaffold is called only once nothing can still refuse — with no unstated exception left for a reader to notice.

The exception itself is gone rather than documented: ADR-0024 removed the wizard's migration arm and with it the post-scaffold collision-retry prompt (LCLI-656), and the four wizard stop paths each assert their write-nothing property against a recursive path-and-content digest (treeDigest), mutant-verified.

implementationNotes:
DISPOSITION, 2026-09-30 (LCLI-519 moved to In Progress on this branch). The task was filed 2026-09-17 against an exception that no longer exists, so its three asks resolve differently than written — recorded here rather than closed quietly, because the description still asserts the exception in the present tense.

Ask 1, "say what makes a post-write prompt legitimate": moot. ADR-0024's implementation (LCLI-656, opum-ai/lore-cli#440) removed the wizard's migration arm, and the prompt LCLI-466 had added after the base scaffold — the interactive collision retry — went with it. There is no post-write prompt left to legitimise.

Ask 2, "update the call-site comment so it stops asserting a universal it no longer has": done as a side effect of the same landing, and checked: src/commands/init.ts:36 now reads "every check now runs before the first byte is written" and names the mechanism (the base scaffold moved into applyBaseScaffold, which both paths call only once nothing can still refuse), and :1344 asserts the same at the write itself without a caveat.

Ask 3, "prefer a check over a comment": done here, at the granularity the ask named. test/init.test.ts carries a prompter that records the directory listing at EVERY prompt boundary and asserts each snapshot is empty, with a positive control in the same invocation so an empty-everything run cannot pass it (created > 0 and prompts recorded > 0), and a mutant run that adds one post-write snapshot turns it red. The four wizard stop paths already carry content-level digests from the same PR (treeDigest, mutant-verified 4 of 4).

No acceptance criteria existed on this record; three were added above so "done" is checkable rather than remembered, and each is checked against a measurement rather than an intention.
